paper.title: What Is It Like to Be a Bat?
paper.zh_title: 成为一只蝙蝠是什么感觉？
paper.author: Thomas Nagel
paper.folder: What Is It Like to Be a Bat 1974
paper.description: 知道蝙蝠的大脑和回声定位机制，能否知道它体验世界的感觉？
paper.note: 本站双语导读，非原文全文或逐句翻译。可与图灵的《计算机器与智能》对照阅读。
paper.rights: 原论文受版权保护，本页仅提供本站编写的双语导读与来源链接。

blocks.en: Imagine knowing a bat's anatomy and the mechanisms of echolocation. Nagel asks whether this objective knowledge gives access to the experience of being that animal.
blocks.zh: 想象我们知道蝙蝠的解剖结构，也明白回声定位的机制。内格尔追问：这些客观知识，是否让我们能够进入作为这种动物的体验？

blocks.en: The problem concerns the point of view carried by conscious experience. Imagining yourself flying in darkness may reveal your imagination without revealing the bat's experience.
blocks.zh: 问题涉及意识体验所带有的视角。想象自己在黑暗中飞行，可能揭示的是你的想象方式，而不是蝙蝠的体验。

blocks.en: Read this beside Turing: a criterion for observable performance and an account of subjective experience address different questions. Their difference makes the pairing productive.
blocks.zh: 可以把它与图灵对照阅读：可观察行为的判定标准，与主观体验的解释，回答的是不同问题。正因为问题不同，两篇放在一起才有启发。

blocks.en: Reading question: what would count as understanding an experience, and whose perspective would that understanding preserve? The article helps formulate the difficulty before offering an easy solution.
blocks.zh: 阅读时可以追问：什么才算理解一种体验？这种理解又保留了谁的视角？文章的价值在于先把困难说清楚，而不是急着给出轻松的答案。
